newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says bank chiefs must declare risks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says bank chiefs must declare risks.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Thursday it has told chief executives of Australian banks they must now file declarations about their bank's risk management, in addition to assurances of auditors, as a way to focus attention of boards on their responsibilities.

"We expect that these declarations, which are due within three months of the end of each bank's financial year, will help focus the attention of boards on their responsibilities for clearly articulating a bank's appetite for risk and then for ensuring that the appropriate framework of risk management is in place," RBA deputy governor Graeme Thompson said in a speech.
Thompson said the RBA wanted to improve arrangements under which auditors provide independent assurances about a bank's management systems for monitoring and controlling risks.
"For some time, we've felt that the auditors' views on the adequacy of banks' systems gave little useful guidance to potential problems," he said.

He said the chief executive's declaration would be endorsed by boards of directors and state that management had identified and established systems to monitor and manage risks which met prudent limits and timely reporting processes.

"The first declaration will be provided by those banks whose financial year ends this month," Thompson said in a speech to a conference hosted by brokerage firm First Pacific. Thompson is in charge of prudential supervision at the central bank.

Three of Australia's largest banks end their financial year on September 30 -- National Australia Bank Ltd, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, and Westpac Banking Corp. Commonwealth Bank of Australia operates on a June year.
The declaration must also provide information to the RBA that is accurate and current, Thompson said.
